summary: The root ZMR relates to making a sound, like playing a reed pipe or the cry of an ostrich. It can also mean to divulge a story or incite someone.
lane: 1 زَمَرَ ذ , aor. زَمِرَ and زَمُرَ , inf. n. زَمْرٌ (S, Msb, K) and زَمِيرٌ (Msb, K) and زَمَرَانٌ ; (ISd, TA;) and , inf. n. تَزْمِيرٌ ; (K;) He [ piped, or] played upon (lit. sang in ) a reed; (K;) he blew in a مِزْمَارٌ . (S, * A, Msb. *) -b2- [Hence,] زَمَرَ النَّعَامُ , (S, K,) and زَمَرَتِ الهَيْقَةُ , (A,) or النَّعَامَةُ , (TA,) aor. زَمِرَ , inf. n. زِمَارٌ (S, A, K) and زُمَارٌ , (TA,) (tropical:) The ostriches, (S, K,) and the she-ostrich, (A, TA,) cried, or uttered their, or her, cry. (S, A, K, TA.) [Said only of the females, or a female:] of the male ostrich one says only عَارَّ . (S, TA.) -b3- And زَمَرَ بِالحَدِيثِ (tropical:) He published, or divulged, the story. (A, K.) -b4- And زَمَرَ فُلَانًا بِفُلَانٍ He excited, or incited, such a one against such a one. (A, * K, TA.) -A2- زَمِرَ , (S, K,) aor. زَمَرَ , (K,) inf. n. زَمَرٌ , (S,) He had little hair, (S, * K, * TA,) and little wool. (K, * TA.) -b2- Also, [hence,] inf. n. as above, (S,) or زَمَارَةٌ and زُمُورَةٌ , (TA,) (tropical:) He (a man, S, TA) had little مُرُوْءَة [i. e. manliness, or manly virtue ]. (S, K.) -b3- And زَمِرَ مَالُهُ , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) His property became little, or scanty. (TA in art. قفر .)

headwords.def: aor. زَمِرَ and زَمُرَ, inf. n. زَمْرٌ (S, Msb, K) and زَمِيرٌ (Msb, K) and زَمَرَانٌ; (ISd, TA;) and, inf. n. تَزْمِيرٌ; (K;) He [ piped, or] played upon (lit. sang in ) a reed; (K;) he blew in a مِزْمَارٌ. (S, * A, Msb. *) [Hence,] زَمَرَ النَّعَامُ, (S, K,) and زَمَرَتِ الهَيْقَةُ, (A,) or النَّعَامَةُ, (TA,) aor. زَمِرَ, inf. n. زِمَارٌ (S, A, K) and زُمَارٌ, (TA,) (tropical:) The ostriches, (S, K,) and the she-ostrich, (A, TA,) cried, or uttered their, or her, cry.
(tropical:) He was, or became, abject, or ignominious, or weak, and small in body, and lean; being abased or brought low. (A, TA.) [See also the part n., below.]

Having little hair; (S, A, K;) and having little wool: fem. with ة. (A, K.) You say صَبِىٌّ زَمِرٌ A child having little hair: and شَاةٌ زَمِرَةٌ [ A sheep, or goat, having little wool or hair ]: and غَنَمٌ زَوَامِرُ [ Sheep, or goats, having little wool or hair ]: (A, TA:) and نَاقَةٌ زَمِرَةٌ A she-camel having little fur: and نَبْتٌ زَمِٰرٌ [app. meaning A plant having few leaves ]. (Ham p. 683.) And شَعَرٌ زَمِرٌ [ Scanty, or thin, hair ].

A company, or congregated body, of men; (S, K;) as also: (TA:) or (so in the TA, but in the K “ and ”) a party in a state of dispersion: (K:) pl. زُمَرٌ: (S, A, K:) you say, جَاؤُوا زُمَرًا They came in parties in a state of dispersion, one after another: (A:) some say that زُمْرَةٌ is from [originally an inf.
Short; (Kr, K;) applied to a man: (TA:) pl. زِمَارٌ. (Kr, K.) And Beautiful; applied to a boy, or young man; (AA, Th, O, K;) as also (AA, O, K) and. (K.) See also زَمِرٌ.
The act [or art ] of [ piping, or] playing upon the reed [ or مِزْمَار ]. (K.)

(As, S, A, Msb, K) and, (As, S, K,) but the latter is rare, (K,) or scarcely ever used, (S,) or it is not allowable, (Msb,) applied to a man; and, (S, Msb, K,) but not زَمَّارَةٌ, (S, Msb,) applied to a woman; (S, Msb, K;) A [ piper, or] player upon a reed; (K;) one who blows in a مِزْمَار. (S, * A, Msb.

[fem. of زَمَّارٌ, q. v. Also] i. q. مِزْمَارٌ, q. v. (K.) And (tropical:) A سَاجُور [i. e. collar, or collar of iron, ] (O, A, K, TA) that is put upon the neck of a dog. (TA.) And metaphorically used as meaning (tropical:) A جَامِعَة; (A, TA;) [i. e.] A [ shackle for the neck and hands, such as is called ] غُلّ. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A bar of iron ( عَمُودٌ ) between the two rings of the [ shackle called ] غُلّ: (M, O, K:) so termed because of its sound.
; and its fem., with ة: see زَمَّارٌ.
: see زُمْرَةٌ: and see also زَمِيرٌ. Also Playing; or a player. (O.)
(assumed tropical:) Shackled [ with a زَمَّارة ]. (O, TA.)

A musical reed, or pipe; (S, * A, Msb, * K, * TA;) what is called in Persian نَاىْ [now generally meaning a flute ]; (marginal note in a copy of the KT;) as also, (K,) [which latter, by many pronounced زُمَّارَة, and generally so pronounced in Egypt, is applied to a double reed-pipe, figured and described in my work on the Modern Egyptians,] and and, (IAth,) the latter like مَغْلُوقٌ and مَغْرُودٌ: (TA:) pl. of the first, (S, A,) and of the last two, مَزَامِيرُ.
and مُزْمُورٌ: see مِزْمَارٌ, in two places.
(tropical:) Shrinking, and abject, or ignominious, in his own estimation. (K, TA.) [See also its verb.]

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
